content: === Introduction ===

This is a complete list of clinically approved prescription antidepressants throughout the world, as well as clinically approved prescription drugs used to augment antidepressants or mood stabilizers, by pharmacological and/or structural classification. Chemical/generic names are listed first, with brand names in parentheses. All drugs listed are approved specifically for major depressive disorder unless noted otherwise.
=== Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) ===
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors include:
=== Serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) ===
Serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors include:
<info> Milnacipran (Ixel, Savella, Milnaneurax)
=== Serotonin–dopamine reuptake inhibitor (SDRIs) ===
Serotonin–dopamine reuptake inhibitors include:
=== Serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitors (SNDRIs) ===
Serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitors include:
=== Serotonin modulators and stimulators (SMSs) ===
Serotonin modulators and stimulators include:
=== Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitors (SARIs) ===
Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitors include:
<info> Nefazodone (Dutonin, Nefadar, Serzone) – withdrawn/discontinued in most countries
=== Norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (NRIs) ===
Norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors include:
<info> Teniloxazine (Lucelan, Metatone) – also a 5-HT2A receptor antagonist
<info> Viloxazine (Qelbree, formerly Vivalan) – also a 5-HT2B receptor antagonist and 5-HT2C receptor agonist
=== Norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitors (NDRIs) ===
Norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitors include:
<info> Bupropion (Wellbutrin, Elontril) – also a non-competitive antagonist of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors[6]
<info> Amphetamines (Adderall, Vyvanse) – actually norepinephrine–dopamine releasing agents (NDRAs)[7][5]
=== Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) ===
<info> Amitriptylinoxide (Amioxid, Ambivalon, Equilibrin)
<info> Melitracen (Dixeran, Melixeran, Trausabun)
<info> Noxiptiline (Agedal, Elronon, Nogedal)

Opipramol (Insidon), tianeptine (Stablon, Coaxil) and amineptine (discontinued; formerly Survector, Maneon) are chemically TCAs but are pharmacodynamically atypical, and are therefore grouped elsewhere.
<info> Iprindole (Prondol, Galatur, Tetran)
<info> Tiazesim (Altinil) – actually not a TCA but a tricyclic-like antidepressant
<info> Tofenacin (Elamol, Tofacine) – actually not a TCA but a tricyclic-like antidepressant
=== Tetracyclic antidepressants (TeCAs) ===
Mianserin, mirtazapine, and setiptiline are also sometimes described as noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressants (NaSSAs).
=== Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) ===
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors include
<info> Selegiline (Eldepryl, Zelapar, Emsam) – also a catecholaminergic activity enhancer and weak norepinephrine releasing agent (via metabolites)
These drugs are sometimes described as reversible inhibitors of MAO-A (RIMAs).
<info> Bifemelane (Alnert, Celeport) – RIMA, irreversible inhibitor of MAO-B, and weak NRI
=== Atypical antipsychotics ===
<info> Amisulpride (Solian) – approved in low doses as a monotherapy for persistent depression and major depressive disorder[10]
<info> Levosulpiride – approved in low doses for major depressive disorder[11]
<info> Lumateperone (Caplyta) – approved as a monotherapy for bipolar depression
<info> Lurasidone (Latuda) – approved as a monotherapy for bipolar depression
<info> Quetiapine (Seroquel) – approved as a monotherapy for bipolar depression
<info> Sulpiride – approved in low doses as a monotherapy for major depressive disorder[12]
=== Others ===
<info> D-Phenylalanine (DPA, D-Phe; Deprenon, Sabiben, Sabiden) – enkephalinase inhibitor
<info> Agomelatine (Valdoxan) – 5-HT2C receptor antagonist and MT1 and MT2 receptor agonist
<info> Brexanolone (allopregnanolone; Zulresso) – GABAA receptor positive allosteric modulator – approved for postpartum depression
<info> Esketamine (Spravato) – non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist, other actions[13]
<info> Gepirone (Exxua) – 5-HT1A receptor partial agonist and α2-adrenergic receptor antagonist
<info> Opipramol (Insidon) — σ1 receptor agonist, other actions
<info> Tianeptine (Stablon, Coaxil, Tianeurax) – weak and atypical μ-opioid receptor agonist, other actions
<info> Ketamine (Ketalar) – non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist[14]
<info> α-Methyltryptamine [αMT] (Indopan) – non-selective serotonin receptor agonist, serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine releasing agent (SNDRA), and weak RIMA
<info> Etryptamine [α-Ethyltryptamine (αET)] (Monase) – non-selective serotonin receptor agonist, SNDRA, and weak RIMA
<info> Indeloxazine (Elen, Noin) – serotonin releasing agent (SRA), NRI, and NMDA receptor antagonist
<info> Oxaflozane (Conflictan) – 5-HT1A, 5-HT2A, and 5-HT2C receptor agonist
<info> Pivagabine (Tonerg) – unknown/unclear mechanism of action
The following antidepressants are available both with a prescription and over-the-counter:
<info> Ademetionine [S-Adenosyl-L-methionine (SAMe)] (Heptral, Transmetil, Samyl) – cofactor in monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis
<info> Hypericum perforatum [St. John's Wort (SJW)] (Jarsin, Kira, Movina) – TRPC6 activator, and various other actions
<info> Oxitriptan [5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP)] (Cincofarm, Levothym, Triptum) – precursor in serotonin biosynthesis
<info> Tryptophan (Tryptan, Optimax, Aminomine) – precursor in serotonin biosynthesis
=== Adjunctive treatments ===
<info> Aripiprazole (Abilify) – approved as an adjunct to antidepressant for major depression
<info> Brexpiprazole (Rexulti) – approved as an adjunct to antidepressant for major depression
<info> Lumateperone (Caplyta) – approved as an adjunct to mood stabilizer for bipolar depression
<info> Lurasidone (Latuda) – approved as an adjunct to mood stabilizer for bipolar depression
<info> Olanzapine (Zyprexa) – approved as an adjunct to antidepressant for major depression
<info> Quetiapine (Seroquel) – approved as an adjunct to antidepressant or mood stabilizer for major depression and bipolar depression
Dopamine reuptake inhibitors include:
<info> Buspirone (Buspar) – 5-HT1A receptor partial agonist
<info> Lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid) – mood stabilizer (mechanism of action unknown/unclear)
<info> Thyroxine (T4) – thyroid hormone (thyroid hormone receptor agonist)
<info> Triiodothyronine (T3) – thyroid hormone (thyroid hormone receptor agonist)
=== Combination products ===
<info> Amitriptyline/chlordiazepoxide (Limbitrol) – TCA and benzodiazepine combination
<info> Amitriptyline/perphenazine (Etafron) – TCA and typical antipsychotic combination
<info> Dextromethorphan/bupropion (Auvelity) – non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist, σ1 receptor agonist, SNRI, NDRI, other actions
<info> Flupentixol/melitracen (Deanxit) – TCA and typical antipsychotic combination
<info> Olanzapine/fluoxetine (Symbyax) – SSRI and atypical antipsychotic combination – approved as a monotherapy for bipolar depression and treatment-resistant depression
<info> Tranylcypromine/trifluoperazine (Parstelin, Parmodalin, Jatrosom N, Stelapar) – MAOI and typical antipsychotic combination
